# ethereum-optimism/optimism Daily Update (Jan 12, 2026)

## OVERVIEW 
Today's development focused on a critical bug fix in `contracts-bedrock` to align compiler restrictions for `StorageSetter`. Several new pull requests were opened, addressing various improvements across the Superchain ecosystem, including upstreaming `op-rs/kona` and enhancing metrics.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### Contract Compiler Alignment
A bug fix was implemented to correct a missing `StorageSetter` setting in the `lite` profile compiler restrictions within `contracts-bedrock`, ensuring proper alignment. ([#18715](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18715))

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
- **Core Infrastructure & Upstream Updates:** A significant effort is underway to upstream `op-rs/kona` to the monorepo ([#18754](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18754)).
- **Developer Tooling & Testing:** New pull requests aim to install `solc` for contracts tests ([#18753](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18753)) and convert `MintManager` tests to fuzz tests for broader coverage ([#18744](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18744)).
- **Feature & Documentation Enhancements:** A new feature proposes moving compatibility validation to a `Features` library ([#18752](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18752)), while documentation is being enhanced with a link to the handbook directory ([#18749](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18749)).
- **Metrics & Service Improvements:** Updates are in progress for `op-supernode` to multiplex metrics by `chain_id` and serve them at a single endpoint ([#18750](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18750)), and `op-service` will now use blob tip cap provided by the blob tip oracle ([#18745](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18745)).

## CLOSED ISSUES
No issues were closed today.

## NEW ISSUES

### Supernode & Interoperability Enhancements
- Integration testing with Interop for `op-supernode` is needed to enable more complex testing scenarios beyond disconnected networks ([#18756](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18756)).
- `op-supernode` should multiplex virtual node metrics with labels instead of URL paths to consolidate metrics at a single endpoint ([#18746](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18746)).

### L2 Client Development
- Support for Osaka-on-L2 needs to be added to `op-reth` ([#18751](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18751)).
- Batcher throttling needs to be implemented in `OP Reth` ([#18747](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18747)).
- A safe head DB needs to be added to Kona ([#18748](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18748)).

### Testing & Validation
- Acceptance tests need to be run against the first Glamsterdam devnet (`bal-devnet-1`) as a dry run to refine tooling and processes ([#18755](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18755)).

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### `op-node`: single aggregate safe-head advancement FCU message per channel ([#15393](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/15393))
The discussion continues regarding the issue of excessive FCU (ForkchoiceUpdated) messages, particularly when the `batcher` runs with a considerable `max-channel-duration`. The latest comment from 0x416e746f6e highlights that a previous attempt to fix this (PR #18385) likely made a mistake, resulting in the current version still performing an FCU on every safe head update instead of buffering them. Earlier comments from teddyknox pointed to a merged PR (#18234) that might help, and clabby noted that `kona-node` has implemented a solution sending only one FCU per span batch in the happy-path. The core problem remains that many FCU calls are made in quick succession, which can be slow if the Execution Layer (EL) is not local, despite being relatively fast for local ELs. There's a suggestion to add a debounce to the engine-controller FCU code, but the impact on overall processing time is debated. The issue also touches on whether FCU calls should be sent with the `no_tx_pool` flag set when they are made so close to each other.
